findings.claim: Replacing the `.vtt` of a loft that already has transcript chunks does not re-index it, so Ask and search keep answering from the old captions although the new `scan.complete` makes it look handled.

For a loft the index is also the only place the correction could show, because known-issues.md records that embeds show no sidecar captions, so the upload has no visible effect. The per-file reindex is the only way out and nothing points to it.

An exception from `os.replace` at complete, for example a target that became a directory or a permission error, leaves the upload session and its temporary directory in place until `cleanup_abandoned_uploads`. This is rare and the shape is pre-existing.

trajectory: Only cde9bc7a3 changes behaviour in this range; 5ea567d60 adds tests, and 4e5d2d82c and f08c2dd63 record the review and R-5. It removes no branch or state and adds one branch, `replaces_subtitle` in `init_upload`, plus an `emit` inside the route's existing subtitle branch. It adds no state and no prediction of disk or name order, so the per-sidecar prediction strand from r1 to r3 and the row-following strand removed in bd49bc092 do not recur. One pattern does repeat. bd49bc092 added a subtitle exception to `complete_upload` and to the route, and this round adds another at `init_upload` and extends the one in the route, so the upload path now treats subtitles differently at each of its stages. On this strand the design is being patched modestly: each exception answers a finding about the one before, because the early return lost the event and the row-less file lost its removal path. The rest of r4's open findings were moved to known-issues.md rather than changed in code, so the record grew by four entries while the code gained one branch. The new findings sit at the edge of the replacement itself: the index does not notice it, it has no undo, and it matches only the exact composed name.
